correctness.rationale: For any finite population at least three and either endpoint mutation parameter, the full Moran transition probabilities and the even/odd reflected minority boundary rows were reconstructed. For fixed mutation the skip-free strong Markov property makes each survival function nondecreasing in minority state. The entrywise nonnegative product rule for \(\partial_\mu Q^t\) acting on these increasing functions, and a strictly positive path from every initial minority level to the leakage state at the earliest possible horizon, prove all finite-horizon inequalities. Primitive Perron theory then yields strictly positive \(\lambda\prime(\mu)\) from the monotone right eigenvector; no numerical finite-set inference is used for the universal quantifiers. The two-individual exception and three-individual closed form are exact. An independent exact-fraction program checks over five thousand finite survival comparisons, over six thousand derivative comparisons, and boundary formulas.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Gaeta provides the same transition probabilities and first-entrance object, but the conclusion on increasing mean time is implied by (and weaker than) the present survival-order theorem; an increasing expectation never implies pointwise stochastic order in general. Huillet may give monotonicity in r for a fixed matrix but not differentiation of Q with respect to symmetric mutation across the first-purity event. Díaz works in fitness/graph comparisons with no further mutations after a parent copy; it does not imply parameter strictness here. Current work proves strictness via the positive derivative of boundary leakage propagated through all finite horizons and separately for the killed Perron rate.

originality.rationale: The 2024 same-model preprint proves or numerically explores first-purity hitting probability and its MEAN with symmetric mutations. The present quantified result concerns strict survival-function inequalities simultaneously for every integer horizon at which purity is attainable, all initial mixtures and all real mutation parameters in the full allowable interval, and strict derivative positivity of a different object: the Perron root of the killed first-entrance kernel. Huillet gives stochastic monotonicity in the state index and full-chain spectral analyses, not this parameter comparison; Díaz et al. prove non-mutating graph-Moran domination. The conclusion is literature-relative, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: General comparison principles for monotone birth–death kernels may have an unindexed formulation whose corollary implies this claim without matching Moran-specific keywords.
Further specialist first-passage or neutral population-genetics literature may contain all-horizon or Perron-order statements not indexed in the searched sources.
No independent literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The motivating biological dynamics question asks how ongoing neutral mutation changes the time to temporary pure populations. Prior plots/recurrences of expected times do not answer the operational question of the chance of having reached purity by a given finite horizon. The new exact structural theorem resolves that natural whole-law question uniformly in population size, starting configuration, and mutation probability, and proves the separate asymptotic spectral-tail effect and a sharp population-size obstruction. Its strict distributional claim is not merely a renaming of an expectation formula or an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
